summary: Visible change: the active entry of the @ and / list (the one Enter or Tab picks, aria-activedescendant) now follows real pointer movement over a row or an entity action. composer.pointerActivation: false (or the RichMentionInput prop) restores the keyboard-only list.
howTo: Nothing to do for the built-in item: it now has a hover look equal to its selected look, only while the pointer drives the list and only on devices with hover. A custom components.DropdownItem (or components.MentionDropdownItem) needs no change; it gets isSelected for the pointer row too. If it has an own :hover style, scope it to [data-component="mention-dropdown"][data-active-source="pointer"] (set while the active entry is the one under the pointer; arrow keys, new results and any scroll of the list set it back to keyboard), or after the arrow keys or a scroll the hovered row and the active row both look marked. A custom item with own pointer handling can call the new optional onActivate() prop, only on real pointer movement, never on mouseenter or mouseover. A custom item that scrolls itself on isSelected also scrolls on pointer activation. Tests that fire pointermove (or, without any pointermove, mousemove) at least 1px away from the last position over the list now move the active entry; the first event after the list opens only records the position. To keep the earlier keyboard-only list, set composer={{ pointerActivation: false }} on AiChatProvider, VercelAiChat or <glirastes-chat> (config.composer); it reaches the built-in composer and useChatComposerInput().inputProps. An own RichMentionInput takes pointerActivation={false}. Then there is no pointer or scroll handling, onActivate does nothing, the listbox has no data-active-source and the built-in stylesheet shows no hover look.
